newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ITC to continue Chile salmon dumping probe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ITC to continue Chile salmon dumping probe.

text.p: The U.S. International Trade Commission voted three to zero on Thursday to continue its probe into accusations Chile has been dumping salmon on the U.S. market.

"There is a reasonable indication that a U.S. industry is materially injured by reason of imports of fresh Atlantic salmon from Chile that are allegedly subsidised and sold in the United States at less than fair value," the ITC said in a statement.

As a result of the vote, the Commerce Department will investigate the allegations made by salmon producers in Maine and Washington to determine whether dumping occurred and if so, how much, the ITC said.

If the department finds evidence to support the claims, the ITC will determine what impact the imports had on the U.S. salmon industry and the department will decide whether sanctions should be enacted, it said.
Chile's exports of salmon and trout to the United States jumped to $177 million in 1996 from just $3.4 million in 1986.
Chilean officials have denied charges that their salmon is subsidised and sold abroad at below-market prices
